\title{Corruption-Aware Image Restoration with Autoencoders, Hard and Soft Expert Routing, and Style-Conditioned Face-to-Sketch Synthesis}

\author{\IEEEauthorblockN{\todo{Student name}}
\IEEEauthorblockA{\todo{Department, University}\\
\todo{e-mail} --- Repository: \url{https://github.com/Ali-prog-spec/Restoration-Sketch-studio}\\
Demo video: \url{\todo{https://youtu.be/VIDEO_ID}}}}

\maketitle

\begin{abstract}
We design, train, evaluate and deploy four generative systems. Tasks~1--3 restore Oxford-IIIT Pet images
corrupted at runtime by salt-and-pepper noise, Gaussian blur or rectangular occlusion: (1)~a single
convolutional denoising autoencoder with a genuine bottleneck, (2)~a corruption classifier that hard-routes
inputs to three specialist autoencoders (with an identity bypass for clean inputs), and (3)~a jointly
fine-tuned soft mixture-of-experts initialised from Task~2. Task~4 is a pix2pix-style conditional GAN that
translates FS2K face photographs into sketches of three styles through a learned style embedding used by
both generator and discriminator. All hyperparameters are tuned with Optuna, all runs are tracked with
MLflow, all deployed models are exported to ONNX and verified numerically, and the four systems are served
by one FastAPI + React application in Docker.

\section{Related Work}
\textbf{Denoising autoencoders.} Vincent et al.~\cite{vincent2008dae,vincent2010sdae} introduced denoising
autoencoders; convolutional encoder--decoders with symmetric skips~\cite{mao2016rednet} and residual
denoisers~\cite{zhang2017dncnn} dominate restoration, but their skip/residual paths bypass the bottleneck
that this assignment requires. Zhao et al.~\cite{zhao2017loss} showed that L1+SSIM-type losses outperform
L2; SSIM is defined in~\cite{wang2004ssim}, PSNR/SSIM trade-offs are discussed in~\cite{hore2010psnr}.
\textbf{Mixture of experts.} Adaptive mixtures of local experts~\cite{jacobs1991moe}; sparsely gated
MoE with importance/load balancing~\cite{shazeer2017moe}; Switch~\cite{fedus2022switch} and
GShard~\cite{lepikhin2021gshard}; temperature-scaled softmax~\cite{hinton2015distill}.
\textbf{Conditional GANs.} GANs~\cite{goodfellow2014gan}, conditional GANs~\cite{mirza2014cgan},
pix2pix with U-Net generator and PatchGAN~\cite{isola2017pix2pix,ronneberger2015unet}, conditioning by
label maps~\cite{choi2018stargan}, conditional normalisation~\cite{devries2017cbn,perez2018film},
projection discriminators~\cite{miyato2018projection}, and perceptual/distributional
metrics~\cite{zhang2018lpips,heusel2017fid}. Hyperparameter optimisation uses Optuna~\cite{akiba2019optuna}
with TPE~\cite{bergstra2011tpe} and median pruning (cf.\ successive halving~\cite{jamieson2016sh,li2018hyperband}).

\section{Dataset Preparation}
\subsection{Oxford-IIIT Pet (Tasks 1--3)}
The official trainval list (3,680 images)~\cite{parkhi2012pets} is split 80/20 with seed 42 into 2,944
training and 736 validation images; the 3,669 official test images are used only for final evaluation.
Images are converted to RGB and resized to $128\times128$. The same split is used by Tasks 1--3
(\texttt{data/manifests/oxford\_split.json}). Source verification of the mirror used for download is
reported in \texttt{oxford\_source\_verification.json}.

\subsection{Corruption configuration}
\begin{table}[t]\centering\caption{Corruption configuration (PDF specification).}\label{tab:corruptions}\small
\begin{tabular}{lll}\toprule
Condition & Training (runtime, uniform) & Test levels (low / med / high)\\\midrule
Clean & original image & -- \\
Salt-and-pepper & $p\sim U(0.02,0.15)$, black/white 50/50 & $p=0.03 / 0.08 / 0.15$\\
Gaussian blur & $k\in\{3,5,7\}$, $\sigma\sim U(0.5,2.5)$ & $(3,0.7)/(5,1.5)/(7,2.5)$\\
Occlusion & 1--3 black rectangles, union 10--35\% & $\approx$10\%/20\%/35\%, 1/2/3 rect.\\\bottomrule
\end{tabular}\end{table}
Training corruptions are sampled every time an image is loaded, with balanced batches ($B/4$ per condition).
Validation (2,944 records) and test (36,690 records) corruptions are stored once in deterministic
manifests (type, level, seed, probability, kernel, $\sigma$, rectangle coordinates, coverage).
\todo{Quote realised occlusion coverage from outputs/tables/manifest\_summary\_test.csv.}

\subsection{FS2K (Task 4)}
The official split (1,058 train / 1,046 test)~\cite{fan2022fs2k} is used; 15\% of train is held out for
validation (stratified by style, seed 42), giving 899/159. Photos and sketches are resized to
$128\times128$; paired augmentation (resize 143, identical random crop and flip) preserves pixel correspondence.

\section{Task 3: Soft Mixture-of-Experts}
\subsection{Architecture and initialisation}
\begin{figure}[t]\centering\artifactfig{arch_moe.pdf}{MoE diagram}
\caption{Soft MoE: gate initialised from the Task 2 classifier, experts from the Task 2 specialists.}\end{figure}
\subsection{Training strategy and joint objective}
$w=\mathrm{softmax}(G(\tilde x)/\tau)$, $\hat x=\sum_k w_k\,b_k(\tilde x)$ and
$\mathcal{L}_{MoE}=\lambda_1\mathcal{L}_{1}+\lambda_s(1-\mathrm{SSIM})+\lambda_c\mathcal{L}_{CE}+\lambda_b\mathcal{L}_{balance}$.
Warm-up with frozen experts, then joint fine-tuning with a smaller learning rate. Balance:
PDF squared loss (equal to Shazeer's CV$^2$ importance loss up to a factor 4) vs.\ marginal-entropy alternative.

\section{Application Architecture}
\begin{figure}[t]\centering\artifactfig{arch_application.pdf}{application diagram}
\caption{Deployment: React/Tailwind frontend (nginx) and FastAPI + ONNX Runtime backend in Docker Compose.}\end{figure}
\subsection{Interface design in Google Stitch}
The interface was first designed in Google Stitch (Figs.~\ref{fig:stitch1}--\ref{fig:stitch2}): a fixed
sidebar listing the four workspaces and the system status page, a header bar, white rounded cards on a
light canvas, an indigo accent colour, monospace labels for technical values, and a two-column workspace
layout (input and corruption controls on the left; an ``inspection stage'' with tagged image panels,
analysis and telemetry cards on the right). These design tokens and components were transferred to the
React/Tailwind implementation (\texttt{frontend/src/index.css}, \texttt{components/ui.jsx},
\texttt{workspaces/*.jsx}); Fig.~\ref{fig:app} shows the implemented application.
\emph{Note:} the Stitch mock-ups contain placeholder content generated by Stitch (e.g.\ face photographs
in Task~1, hardware names, model names and metric values); these are not results of this project. Only
the visual design was adopted; every value shown by the implemented application comes from the backend.
